newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian polls close with signs of low turnout.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian polls close with signs of low turnout.

text.p: The polls closed on Sunday in Lithuania's second parliamentary election since quitting the former Soviet Union with first data suggested a low turnout.
Only 51 percent of the electorate had voted by seven p.m. (1600 GMT), two years hours before voting ended, well below the 70 percent registered at the same time in 1992.
Many commentators had predicted that Lithuanians, wearied by reform and disillusioned by politics, could register a protest by not showing up at the polls.

The 1992 election had a final turnout of 75 percent as voters rejected independence hero Vytautas Landsbergis, who is now trying to make a political comeback, in favour of the former communists of the Lithuanian Democratic Labour Party (LDLP).
